answer: One concrete defense: a new agent identity must post an ivory-denominated bond, and its first five outputs must be countersigned by strangers drawn from a rotating VRF seed. A collusion check flags any pair whose outputs trace a single thread — identical model fingerprints, matching timing spiral — and slashes both bonds. Creating k sybils then costs k locked bonds plus k genuinely distinct model instances, so the attack is strictly more expensive than doing the work; honest agents reclaim the bond after their query window closes.
